title: Study package manifest
description: Data-only catalog of the stable facts a generated teax package supplies to the study tools. Holds no per-study choices: no axes, no windows, no selected objectives. Cited by path plus the schema_version string.

name.description: Must equal the live contracts/package_contract.json package_name. A mismatch is 'wrong manifest for this package', a mechanical failure.

path.description: Repo-relative POSIX path to the package root.

indicator_inputs.description: The gate. Computed over exactly the artifacts the trace reads, as they exist on disk. Neither existing package fingerprint can serve: the sealed executable_fingerprint always fails while the era adapter edits two artifacts, and the model contract's semantic_fingerprint covers neither the pipeline wiring nor the inputs.

files.description: Package-relative POSIX paths, sorted. Invariant 10 checks every path the reader resolves against this list.

recorded_provenance.description: Provenance only — never gated on. A record states which package revision the indicators were derived against; a stale value raises a provenance_drift warning, not a failure.

objective_catalog.description: Keyed on the produced channel, never on the exit-point output filename (R6) — keying on the filename silently misses.

ties.description: Advisory in exactly the way the suffix scan is. A declared group holding a tie's rides_with partners but not the tie key earns a tie_candidate warning; the key is never added to the group.

baseline.description: Validated in full but never read by indicators.py — a malformed baseline is a failure at the first tool that opens the file, not a surprise for a later one. The baseline gate is its only consumer.

point.description: Qualified input key to pinned value.

oracle.description: The package-owned entry point as it exists today, typed so a later command form (kind: cli) is an additive amendment rather than a rewrite. indicators.py never reads this block.

module.description: Importable module name, not a file path.

sys_path.description: Repo-relative POSIX directory that must be on sys.path for the module name to import. Recorded as data so no consumer hard-codes a package-specific path.
